Commentary.Commentary: With that, we come to an end of this thrilling contest. The focus now shifts to Melbourne where the Boxing Day Test will be held on 26th December at the MCG. Do join us for that one. Until then, it's goodbye from us. Hop on to the India-England tab for the updates. Cheers!

STEVEN SMITH accepts that it got too close for comfort in the end. Praises Pakistan for putting up a really great fight. Says that his bowlers worked hard and praises Starc for producing that special delivery to remove Shafiq with an old soft ball. Denies that they were worried about losing although they were tensed. Defends his decision not to enforce the follow-on and says that he doesn't regret it. Lauds Pakistan's batsmen once more for the fight. Feels that the Day/Night Test concept is nice although this was too close for his comfort eventually.

MISBAH-UL-HAQ admits that it was a really nervy finish but still maintains that he is happy with the fight shown especially after the first innings debacle. Praises all the batsmen, particularly Shafiq and the tail for not giving up. Maintains that he believed that his team could do it coming into the final day. Feels that Wahab's wicket was crucial but still says that he kept believing. Adds that his team kept hope till the last wicket fell. Concludes by saying that his team is looking forward to the next Test.

ASAD SHAFIQ (PLAYER OF THE MATCH) thanks God for all the blessings. Says that he was due for a big knock as he had been hitting it well in the nets. Praises the lower order for showing an amazing fight and giving him support. Says that he wasn't tired today despite the heroics yesterday. Accepts that it was a great delivery from Starc and that he didn't expect it from the pacer at that stage.

Australia's pacers had a good game with Starc being the standout performer. He struck vital blows and his fitness level was laudable. Amir and Wahab had a good game for Pakistan with both bat and ball. Overall, Australia would be pleased at having crossed the line but it certainly was a real scare for them. Pakistan will get confidence going into the crucial Boxing Day Test. AUSTRALIA'S 28-YEAR UNBEATEN RECORD AT THE GABBA CONTINUES.

Pakistan did manage to get to 142 courtesy Sarfraz and Amir but importantly, kept the Aussies a bit more longer on the field and that influenced Smith's debatable call not to enforce the follow-on. The Australians racked up quick runs through Smith and Khawaja to set Pakistan a target that looked improbable but almost became probable in the end. Such is the uncertainty of this game. High quality entertainment it was for sure.

Wahab's dismissal in the final over of day probably was vital as it just calmed Australia. Shafiq however marched on even after getting his century and found able support from Yasir. The required runs came below 50 and pressure rose before a Starc special dislodged Shafiq to settle the game. It looked very rosy for the Aussies over the first two days. Centuries from Smith and Handscomb had propelled them to a challenging score before their bowlers reduced Pakistan to 67/8.

What an absolute cracker of a game! Pakistan looked dead and buried on day two but have then fought back amazingly to go down fighting. Chasing a mammoth target of 490, Azhar and Younis set the platform yesterday but it didn't seem like the visitors were going for the target. However, things changed once Shafiq and the guys below him joined forces. Sarfraz and Amir counterattacked to give the visitors serious belief while Wahab too dug in.

It was a very full ball on off, Yasir just about kept it out towards second slip on the bounce but in the process had gone out of his crease. Smith collects the ball and is alert enough to fire a direct hit at the keeper's end. No doubt at that as Yasir was well short. What an anti-climax but it's been one heck of a contest for sure! Australia looked desperate to end the game today as concerns about the weather loom large. Also, Pakistan has made a supreme effort and now need 108 runs with 2 wickets remaining. While the odds are still not in the visitors' favor, the day ended on a high note for Pakistan with victory not seeming such a distant possibility. Join us tomorrow for the conclusion of this rather dramatic Test. Australia will look to wrap it up quickly while Pakistan will attempt the impossible and look to draw or even win the match. Till tomorrow, goodbye and take care!

Asad Shafiq was able to pick up the pace when partnered with Mohammad Amir who was promoted and nearly scored his maiden Test 50. He is now partnered by the penultimate batsman, Yasir Shah who is holding up his end of the partnership. Starc, Bird took three wickets and Nathan Lyon, picked up two, with each bowler delivering excellent performances.

Earlier in the day, Azhar Ali and Younis Khan extended their partnership to 91 runs. Ali scored a stubborn 71 while Younis played a rapid game of catch up before getting dismissed for 65. A few quick wickets and Pakistan were in a shaky position but Asad Shafiq came in to stabilize the innings. He stayed on in a remarkable innings and remains unbeaten on 100. Along the way, he found a suitable partner in Sarfraz Ahmed.

A determined fightback from Pakistan sees them make great progress towards what originally looked to be a very daunting target. The Australian pacers seemed to lose some of their effectiveness in the night session, leaking runs at a constant pace. Bird was the standout bowler of the session, consistent in his line and length while Starc added a measure of ferocity as both bagged a triple.

Starc is a happy man but Smith looks even happier.

DROPPED! It's Steven Smith would you believe it? Length ball outside off, Sarfraz pokes at it and gets a thick outside which flies to Smith quickly at second slip. The Australian captain fails to grab it and Sarfraz Ahmed gets a life. It came at an awkward height, near chest high for Steven Smith.

...Day 4, Session 3...

So Australia need five more wickets to win this Test. Don't forget, the final session will be under lights and there are high chances it could turn out to be the final session of the Test. Join us back in a bit to catch the action.

Good session for Australia as they picked up three big wickets. We had a delayed start to the second session but after that the Australians bowled much better to take the wickets. Starc's short ball plan worked as he removed Azhar Ali. This was followed by Misbah-ul-Haq, who got out to Bird for another cheap score. Younis Khan batted well today but played a rather poor shot and got out to Lyon, giving Australia complete control in this match.
Fuller length ball on off, Sarfraz works it through mid-wicket and takes three runs. That will be DINNER ON DAY 4!

TEA TAKEN! Due to storm warning, the officials have decided to take early Tea! So that was a good session for Pakistan. They didn't lose a single wicket and battled it out. DROPPED? On middle and leg, Ali looks to sweep and the ball goes off the glove. The ball goes off Wade's gloves too behind and runs to the fine leg fence. Single taken.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Around off, YK drives it towards mid on.
Outside off, Khan square cuts it. Once more, the fielder's efforts pay off as the batsmen are just able to get a single out of it.

Length ball outside off, played with soft hands as YK edges it behind point.
Full on off, defended with a straight bat.

Outside off, Ali gets down and sweeps it through square leg for a single.
Flighted outside off, driven through mid off.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Fullish ball, defended off the front foot with a straight bat.
Close one! Length ball outside off, the ball goes off the outside edge of Younis Khan's defense. It falls just short of the waiting hands at second slip and he gets away with it.
FOUR! Flashed! Good length ball outside off, Younis looks to punch it again but gets an outside edge. That makes it through the slips and YK gets a boundary for it.
Shortish ball outside off, punched to the covers. The batsmen take a single and a throw from the fielder at the batsman's end hits the stumps. The batsmen decide against taking another run.
Fullish delivery around off, pushed to mid-wicket.

Flighted outside off, defended with the full face of the bat.

Down the leg side, YK thinks to play it but lets it through.
Good length delivery outside off, left alone.
Shorter ball outside off, punched through point.
Back of a length ball on off, Younis stands tall and defended to short mid-wicket.
Length ball outside off, played to point off the back foot.
Fullish ball outside off, defended with soft hands to the off side.
Landed outside off, Ali defends it off his back foot.
On middle and off, Ali pushes it towards mid on.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full on off, Azhar strides forward and pushes it to mid on.

Flatter outside off, Younis tries to defend but gets a bit of an inside edge onto his pads. The ball goes to the off side and Lyon almost turns around to get back to his bowling mark but Younis realizes there is no one picking up the ball and the batsmen quickly take a single.
Around off, Azhar comes forward and drives it through mid on for a single.
Nathan Lyon to bowl now.
BEATEN! Good length ball outside off, nips back in sharply, Younis tries to defend but the ball cuts him into two halves and just beats his inside edge.

Wide outside off, Younis leaves it alone.
Back of a length ball on off, Younis taps it to the off side and looks for a single but they don't take it.
Fullish outside off, Ali drives it towards mid on yet again.

Azhar is standing with the on-field physios after getting struck near the neck. He is smiling a bit, so it doesn't seem to be serious.
Banged in short, Ali tries to duck under it but fails to do so and gets hit flush on the helmet. He looks okay, thankfully.
Landed outside off, Ali tries to push but gets squared up and gets an outside edge towards second slip.
Good length ball outside off, Ali defends it into the ground.

EDGED! Short of a length ball on off, Younis stands tall in his style and tries to fend but gets an outside edge which falls short of the gully fielder.

Shortish outside off, Younis punches it towards point.
Full delivery on the off stump, driven to mid on.
Shortish ball outside off, AA springs up to defend it off the back foot.
Fullish ball outside off, defended off the back foot to the off side.
Length ball on middle and leg, flicked to mid-wicket. That was a well-timed shot and the batsman earns three runs from it.
Full delivery outside off, defended back to the bowler.
Bouncer! Younis is quick to react, bending his knees a bit to avoid it.
Just about down the leg side, Ali tries flicking it but misses.

Wide outside off, left alone.
Full delivery on middle,  Azhar switches up quickly to clip it to mid-wicket.
Back of a length ball outside off, Azhar is comfortable shouldering his arms to that one.
Younis has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Length ball outside off, Younis steps forward to play it but the ball takes an inside edge and he is struck on the thigh pad.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under the bouncer at the last moment.

Just safe! Short ball on middle and leg, Khan looks to pull it. He isn't in control of the shot as it takes a top edge. The ball makes it just over the fielder's head and goes to fine leg for a brace.
Length ball on off, defended off the front foot to the off side.
Full and outside off, defended with soft hands to the off side.
Short ball on the stumps, YK goes back and looks to fend it off with a straight bat for a single. The ball goes off his gloves and goes through square leg. Good ball to finish the over.
Younis steps forward once more, defending the length delivery to point.
Outside off, pushed to the off side off the front foot.
Fullish delivery on off, defended to point.
In the corridor outside off, left alone.
Length ball outside off, driven through mid off.

Full and a tad outside off, Younis steps forward and drives it through the covers. That's a beautiful shot but he doesn't get enough power behind to it get it to the boundary. The batsmen run fast enough to get a triple.
Good length delivery on off, Younis looks to defend it and gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Length ball on off, defended behind the line of the delivery.

Bouncer! Younis ducks to let it over.

The floodlights are on at the 'Gabba as it's gone really dark out there.
EDGED AGAIN! Length ball on off, Younis tries to defend but gets an outside edge which falls short of the slip fielder.

FOUR! EDGED! Younis Khan is finally off the mark! Length ball on off, YK tries to defend but gets a thick outside edge. The ball goes through the slip region and races away to the fence. Younis will be relieved as he has avoided a pair.
Mitchell Starc to bowl from the other end.
Length ball outside off, Ali tries to defend but gets a bit of an inside edge onto his pads.
Landed outside off, Ali doesn't play at it.
Fuller length ball on off, Azhar flicks it towards mid-wicket.

The players are out in the middle. Azhar Ali and Younis Khan stride out to bat. Josh Hazlewood who bowled beautifully yesterday, to start the proceedings.

The target is still a massive one and a lot depends on Azhar Ali, currently on 41, to hold up Pakistan's side of things. The weather might side with the visitors as there are showers expected late in the day, giving them a chance to draw the match, since a win for them at this stage seems unlikely.

Hello and welcome to Day 4 of the first Test between Australia and Pakistan. Australia will be ready to begin the day afresh and look to make early inroads into the Pakistan's line-up. With two wickets down, they will be eager to pick up a few more before the visitors settle in.
...Day 4, Session 1...

Australia will be happy with the way they bowled. The ball was not doing much and they leaked a few runs early on but then got into their groove as they stifled the run-rate. They will look to come back tomorrow afresh and try and finish the game on Sunday itself. The forecast is not that promising for Sunday and Pakistan will hope that they get a chance to celebrate that day in the team hotel. Join us at 0830 IST (0300 GMT) for all the action from Day 4. You can also catch all the action from the India-England Test match. Adios! Take Care!
Younis Khan has had a few nervous moments but he has survived those, albeit he is yet to get off the mark. Azhar Ali got a few boundaries before close which puts him in good stead for tomorrow.

The intent was positive from the openers. Sami Aslam and Azhar Ali got a few boundaries to start the innings and added 31 for the opening wicket, before the former nicked one behind to Renshaw at first slip off Starc. Then, all of a sudden, the run-rate dipped as Azhar and Azam simply could not get the ball away. Eventually, the latter got consumed in the bottleneck and edged one to Smith at first slip off Lyon.

A much better reply from Pakistan in comparison to their first innings. They have lost only two wickets in probably the toughest conditions to play cricket. They are not out of the woods by any means, but at least, they have fought hard.

A fine shot to end the day. Full and outside off, Azhar drives this straight down the ground. David Warner gives it a good chase from mid off and finally manages to get to the ball. Slides, tries to collect but ends up pushing it back. The batsmen take the third on that fumble. STUMPS ON DAY 3!
Landed outside off, Azhar takes his bat out of the way.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Pushes it towards gully.
Outside off, Azhar defends it to the off side.
On a good length around off, pushed towards mid on.
Should be the last over of the evening...
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.
A bouncer to test his footwork, Khan ducks.
Full and around off, swinging in, Younis looks to drive but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and around off, watchfully kept out.
FOUR! Third in the over! What an over to watch. Full and outside off, Azhar leans and drives it through mid off and cover again. Warner chases it once more but cannot get there!

FOUR! He does it again! This time a bit closer towards mid off. Full and outside off, Azhar leans again and executes another cover drive, this time towards widish long off. Warner gives it a chase once more but finishes second best.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Awesome! Full and wide outside off, Azhar leans and drives it through the covers for a boundary! Warner gives it a chase from mid off but the ball wins the race.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, Ali goes back and makes it into a yorker as he digs it to the off side.
JACKSON BIRD comes on for a final burst before stumps.

ALMOST! Hazlewood is well on top of Younis at the moment. Pitches this up to the batsman, Younis looks to drive it straight, or through mid on but is beaten all ends up. Hazlewood has a quiet word or two with Younis.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
This one swings back in a long way, YK manages to flick it to short mid-wicket.
A short ball around middle, Younis looks to tuck it away but the ball goes off his gloves to the leg side.
Full and outside off, Khan pushes it tentatively towards point.
What a beauty. Landed on a length outside off, Younis looks to play it through the leg side but the ball seams away to beat the outside edge.
Comes over the wicket now and bowls it outside off, driven towards mid on. Lyon rushes to his right to stop.
Goes back and works it towards short leg.
Comes around the wicket, bowls it on middle, Azhar comes down the track and pushes it back to the bowler.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Outside off, watchfully defended.

Full and outside off, pushed towards mid off.

Landed outside off, worked straight to mid-wicket.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Pushes it towards mid on.
Full and around off, defended with his head right on top of the ball.
YOUNIS KHAN walks in at number 4, replacing Azam.

OUT! Edged and taken! Full and wide outside off, Azam draws to push but the ball straightens a touch and takes the outside edge. Smith takes it nicely at first slip. The change of ball has done the trick. The break has got a wicket for the Australians. End of a sluggish stand.

Steven Smith is not happy with the shape of the ball. The umpires check it, have a discussion, push it through the 8-shaped gauge. It goes through one, does not go through the other. Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.

Landed outside off, spinning in, Azam stays back to defend but misses and is hit on the pads. Lyon appeals but the umpire shakes his head. Warner wants it reviewed but Lyon says no. Hawk Eye shows the impact to be outside off and the ball to be spinning over the stumps.
Works this straight to short mid-wicket.

The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

NOT OUT. Down the leg side, Azam looks to flick but misses. Wade appeals for a catch but the umpire tuns it down. Smith asks Wade about the review, he is not sure, yet he goes for the review. Hot Spot detects nothing, Snickometer detects nothing either. Australia lose a review.
We have a review here for a caught behind. No one seems confident, yet, Smith has gone for the review.
Landed outside off, spinning in, worked straight to square leg.
Same line, probing outside off, avenue of apprehension, AA lunges and lets the ball go.

Outside off, pushed down to an unexplained long on for a run.

Fuller and closer to the off stump, flicked nicely through mid-wicket for a single.
Tossed up wide outside off, spinning in, Azam gets a long stride forward and lets it through.
Similar line and length, left alone.
Play and a miss. That was how most of the wickets fell in the first innings for Pakistan. Full and outside off, drawing the batsman forward, Azhar pushes but misses.
Full and around off, pushed towards mid on.

On a length wide outside off, perhaps a gentle loosener, left alone.

Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.

The batsman picked that bouncer early and let it through to the keeper.
Full and wide outside off, left alone.

Oho... this is very rare and strange. Nic Maddinson at leg slip is standing exactly at the same position where Matthew Wade is standing. I mean, usually, slips stand either in front or behind the keeper, so that they do not collide while diving for the catch.

I might be calling this too early but Michael Clarke is filling the resume for the post of the Australian coach. The way he is observing or has observed Starc is terrific. To the detail. Just like a coach will look at his bowler. Clarke opines that Starc is bowling fast but he is not at his best. Because, when he is at his best, his front foot slides across the popping crease. However, here, his front foot is well inside the line. Excellent observation, sir. Take a bow. Magnificent insight.

Outside off, left alone.

Landed around off, defended towards short mid-wicket.

Outside off, pushed back to the bowler.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, Azhar gets across and pushes it towards mid on.
Length ball outside off, it's left alone for the keeper to collect.
Very solid in defense is Sami Aslam. Shows technique as he walks across to cover the line and present a beautiful, straight bat.
Similar ball, similar defended. Solidly done I might add.
From around the wicket now to Sami Aslam, it's a length ball angling in from around off, the left-hander stays perfectly behind the line to tap it softly on the off side.
Good ball and equally well played too. Bird fires in a yorker and gets it to swing in on middle and leg, Azhar Ali flicks it through mid-wicket and gets three runs to his name. Nicely done.
Starts off with a length delivery and bowls it on the fifth stump line, Ali leans forward and defends it in front of covers.
JACKSON BIRD comes into the bowling attack.

On a good length but it's well outside off, no trouble for the batsman to not have anything to do with it.
Good delivery. Nice line, nice length and it's at a good speed too. In the corridor of uncertainty, Sami Aslam does well however to walk across and meet it with a straight blade.
Hits the deck hard and bangs it in short, angling in on middle and leg, Sami Aslam ducks really early and lets the ball sail over him.
Tight defense from the southpaw, he keeps his bat and pad very close and comfortably keeps it out.
Hazlewood switches angles and comes from around the wicket, pounds in a back of a length delivery outside off, it's blocked out square on the off side.
Top line. Angles it across in the channel outside off, Azhar Ali leans across and with a perfectly straight blade, blocks it back down the track to end the over.
A bit too straight from Mitchell Starc, bowls it on Azhar Ali's thigh pad. No trouble for the opener to close his body up a bit and work it gently on the on side.
Keeps it on the shorter side and bowls this very close to the off pole, it's kept out rather solidly by the right-hander.
Fuller length ball outside off, Aslam with a solid punch as he leans ahead. Picks up a run as the fielder chases it down and throws it back in Wade's direction.

Starc comes charging in and fires it full outside off, Azhar Ali reaches out and drives it towards the covers. Scurries to the other end and picks up a quick single for it. Good running.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under the bouncer at the last moment.
Great line from Hazlewood, keeps it in that channel outside off, Aslam shoulders his arms to that one.
Back of a length outside off, going away from the southpaw opener, he raises his bat skywards and lets it through.
Length delivery aiming the top of off stump, Sami Aslam leans across, gets behind the line and keeps it out from within his crease.
Angling across the left-hander, it's on a length and outside off, left alone for the keeper to collect.
Full and swinging in on middle and leg, Azhar drives it to the right of the mid on fielder. Picks up a single for doing so.
An edge which doesn't carry. On middle and leg, Sami Aslam gets a leading edge towards the covers as he closes the face a little too early. Luckily for him, it falls safely.
Good timing on that shot. Fuller length ball outside off, Azhar Ali drives it through the covers. Doesn't get all of it but it's enough to get him three good runs. Lovely shot.
Homing in on the pads, wristed away to mid on for no run.
FOUR! That's a bit dangerous from Azhar Ali. He's played with a slightly open face and this length ball goes off the outer half past the slip cordon for a boundary.
Length ball angling in to the pads, Aslam picks it up and flicks it through backward square leg for three good runs.

Landed outside off, comes back in a long way, left alone.
This is outside off, comes back in, Azhar just gets his bat down in time, in front of his pad and defends it, with an open bat face towards cover-point.
Full and outside off, defended watchfully.
Landed outside off, let through again.
